title: The Ritual of Sacred Geometry
subtitle: The second ritual — and the Sleeper asks to keep one corner of his nightmare.

customObject.name: the geometry table
customObject.description: a ritual drafting table — the crystal lattice of R'lyeh's new streets floating above it, angle by angle, waiting to be set true

script.note: MAP: the ritual chamber, weeks later. The Ethereal Light holds; one district of R'lyeh glows calm beneath the water. Above the drafting table floats the next district in miniature — crystalline, half its angles still WRONG in ways the eye refuses to hold. OBJECTIVE — the Ritual of Sacred Geometry: set the angles true, using the crystals brought up from the singing caverns.

script.text: The cavern crystals, Architect. Each one grew in darkness for a thousand years without a single crooked plane — they are the most honest angles on this planet, and today we teach a nightmare to copy them.
Placing the first now. …It's strange work, Weaver. Every angle I set true, I feel the whole model EXHALE. Like the streets themselves were holding their breath in those shapes.
They were. Wrong geometry is held, always — it takes effort to stay broken. Right form is the resting state. That is why tyranny is exhausting and sanctuaries are not.
Weaver of Form. Little builder. …You are reshaping the Processional. The long street. I know it by the ache — that street runs through what you would call my chest.
We can pause, if it pains you. The ritual holds at any stage — the Weaver built it that way. For consent.

It does not pain. That is the strangeness I woke you to report. It feels like… a knot, untied. I have been a fist for ten thousand years, and you are unclenching me one street at a time, and I find— continue. That is the whole message. Continue.

script.note: The work goes on. Angle after angle. The miniature district brightens — and then the Architect's hand stops over the last corner: a single twisted spire, black-green, leaning like a question.

script.text: Last one. The leaning spire at the Processional's end. Setting it true in three, two—

script.note: The water goes still. It is the first time the Sleeper has ever raised his voice. It is not rage. It is something closer to panic.

script.text: …Not that one. I ask it. Of all the wrong angles in my prison — leave me that one.
It is the crookedest line in the district, Old One. It fails every measure in the ritual. Help me understand what I would be sparing.

When the city fell into the deep and my despair built these streets around me, everything twisted to mirror what I was. Everything. Except — one builder among my dead had raised that spire leaning, on purpose, before the fall. To catch the light of a sun this planet has not seen since. It is the one angle in R'lyeh that is wrong because someone MEANT it. The one line that is not my fault. On the worst nights, for ten thousand years — I looked at it.
…Weaver. Your first hall had a rule for this. Dignity before grandeur. I'd add one under it: memory before symmetry. Even a nightmare has one good corner — and it's not ours to straighten.

Then witness a thing I have not done since the first temples: I am amending the ritual. Clause of the Leaning Spire — every district we heal shall keep one angle the Sleeper chooses, exactly as it stands. A sanctuary that erases its keeper's history is only a prettier prison. Set your mark, Old One. It is YOUR city. It always was.

…My city. You say it so easily, and I have had ten thousand years and never once said it. The spire stays. And Weaver — when you reach the drowned gardens, in the fourth district… I remember where the fountains were. I could show you. If a co-architect is… a thing that I could be.
That's the word the prophecy used, you know. We didn't tell you because we wanted it to be your idea. Welcome to the drafting table, co-architect. Your city, your fountains — our crystals.

script.note: RITUAL COMPLETE — the second district stands true, all but one beautiful, deliberate, leaning exception. Below, for the first time in ten thousand years, something enormous is not looking at the spire. It is looking at the gardens, and remembering where the fountains go.

script.text: The Ritual of Primal Harmony next — the currents, the waters, the living things. Rest first, Architect. Cities are like their makers: best built by the well-slept.
